hyps.why: Removing the direct edge is worse when another input-output path is also missing.
Another conv into node 3 reduces the marginal benefit of a conv on edge 3.
With the direct edge absent, edge 5 carries more of the output's information, so its conv matters more.
Edge 1 reaches the output only through edge 5, so with edge 5 removed its conv is wasted.
With edge 4 missing, edge 0 can only reach the output through the longer 1->2->3 route.
Edge 2 conv is useful when edge 5 carries a conv onward to the output.
Edge 4 reads node 1, which is only fed by edge 0, so with edge 0 absent the conv is useless.
Diminishing returns: a parallel conv path into the output already exists.
Cutting edge 3 is more damaging when edge 5 is also absent, leaving fewer paths to the output.
Without edge 0, node 1 is empty so edge 2 gets no input and its conv is useless.
